newsitem.title: USA: U.S. equity funds rise 2.61 pct in Q3 - Lipper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. equity funds rise 2.61 pct in Q3 - Lipper.

text.p: Returns of U.S. equity mutual funds increased 2.61 percent in the third quarter, despite a dismal July in which the average fund declined by 6.08 percent, Lipper Analytical Services Inc. said Wednesday.
The top performing sector was financial services, which gained 7.64 percent in the quarter.

"Mergers and acqusitions among some leading banks sparked the biggest gains," Lipper said in a statement. Lipper cited Chase Manhattan Corp. rising after it closed its merger with Chemical Bank and NationsBank Corp.'s agreement to buy Boatmen's Boatmen's Bancshares Inc. as key factors.
Total return is defined as a change in the net asset value of the fund combined with dividends and capital gains distributions.
Science and technology funds returned 5.62 percent. Lipper noted the sector has been able to recover from steep losses in the fourth quarter of 1995.

Michael Lipper, the president of the firm, said, however, he was cautious toward the sector, noting in a statement that the market was rewarding only selected issues rather than pushing all technology segments higher.

Real estate funds also put in a strong performance, rising 5.75 percent in the quarter. Lipper said strength in the sector "always raises the question of whether investors are worried about inflation, but the evidence is mixed."
One barometer, gold funds, fell 2.01 percent in the period, while another yardstick, natural resources funds, rose 4.09 percent.

Growth funds rose 2.90 percent, small company growth funds were up 1.75 percent, S&P 500 index funds increased 2.95 percent, growth and income funds were up 2.90 and equity income funds added 2.66 percent.
World equity funds underperformed their U.S. brethren, dropping 0.73 percent, and Japanese funds fell 6.37 percent.
